facts.statement: Fossils of Tianyuraptor were discovered in western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Its remains have been found in western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Tianyuraptor is a short-armed dromaeosaurid dinosaur closely related to birds.
facts.quote: Tianyuraptor is a genus of short-armed dromaeosaurid dinosaur ('running lizard'; a type of small dinosaur considered to be closely related to birds)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, STM1–3, is a nearly complete skeleton missing only the very tip of the tail.
facts.quote: The type specimen is STM1–3, a nearly complete and fully articulated skeleton that is only missing the extreme distal end of the tail.

facts.statement: The nearly complete holotype skeleton of Tianyuraptor is estimated to be 1.8 meters long.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, STM1–3, un esqueleto casi entero y completamente articulado al que le falta solamente el extremo distal de la cola, lo que le da un estimado de 1,8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The fossil preserves 25 fully articulated tail vertebrae, with at most three more estimated to be missing from the end.
facts.quote: A total of 25 fully articulated caudal vertebrae are preserved and at the end three at most are estimated to be missing.

facts.statement: Unlike many other theropods from the Jehol Group, the Tianyuraptor holotype preserves no soft tissues.
facts.quote: The holotype of Tianyuraptor preserves no soft tissues, unlike many other theropod specimens from the Jehol Group.

facts.statement: Tianyuraptor's forelimbs are unusually short, measuring only 53% of the length of its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: The forelimbs are comparatively short, being only 53% of the hindlimbs' length.

facts.statement: The tail of Tianyuraptor is relatively long, measuring 960 mm and nearly 4.8 times the length of the femur.
facts.quote: As in other dromaeosaurid fossils discovered in Liaoning, the tail is relatively long at 960 mm, nearly 4.8 times as long as the femur.

facts.statement: Tianyuraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: Tianyuraptor is a genus of short-armed dromaeosaurid dinosaur ('running lizard'; a type of small dinosaur considered to be closely related to birds) that lived during the Early Cretaceous, about 122 million years ago.

facts.statement: The specific rock layer where Tianyuraptor fossils were found, the Dawangzhangzi Bed, is dated to about 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Dawangzhangzi Bed specifically has been dated to about 122 million years ago.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tianyuraptor is a basal microraptorine or a basal member of the clade containing other Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: However, it is also equally possible, as argued by Zheng et al., that Tianyuraptor may in fact be a basal member of a clade containing all other Laurasian dromaeosaurids with the exception of Microraptorinae.

facts.statement: In 2013, Agnolín and Novas interpreted Tianyuraptor as an averaptoran of uncertain position.
facts.quote: Agnolín and Novas interpreted the taxon as an averaptoran of uncertain position in 2013.

facts.statement: The species name ostromi honors John Ostrom, a significant contributor to the study of dromaeosaurid fossils.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, ostromi, is in honor of John Ostrom, who contributed greatly to the study of dromaeosaurid fossils, including Deinonychus and feathered dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Tianyuraptor had forelimbs that were only 53% the length of its hind limbs.
facts.quote: Los miembros superiores son comparativamente cortos con respecto a los miembros traseros, midiendo solamente 53% de la longitud de estos últimos.

facts.statement: The ratio of the tibiotarsus to the femur in Tianyuraptor was 1.30.
facts.quote: Tianyuraptor tiene un cociente entre el tibiotarso y fémur de 1,30

facts.statement: The ratio of the arm length to leg length in Tianyuraptor was approximately 0.53.
facts.quote: mientras que Tianyuraptor tiene uno de 0,53

facts.statement: The type specimen of Tianyuraptor was formally described in 2009.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, descrito formalmente en 2009

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in the Dawangzhangzi Bed of the Yixian Formation in Lingyuan, western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: El fósil fue descubierto en el Lecho Dawangzhangzi de la Formación Yixian, parte del Grupo Jehol, ubicado en Lingyuan en el oeste de Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The Yixian Formation, where Tianyuraptor fossils were found, dates from approximately 129.7 to 122.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: La Formación Yixian es una unidad de roca del Cretácico Inferior, fechada entre aproximadamente 129,7 y 122,1 millones de años

facts.statement: The Dawangzhangzi Bed specifically dates to approximately 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: La Formación El Lecho Dawangzhangzi específicamente ha sido datado hace 122 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: The type specimen, STM1-3, is an almost complete and articulated skeleton missing only the distal end of the tail.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo es STM1–3, un esqueleto casi completo y totalmente articulado al que solo le falta el extremo distal de la cola.

facts.statement: The type specimen preserves a total of 25 fully articulated caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Se conservan un total de 25 vértebras caudales completamente articuladas

facts.statement: Researchers believe the type specimen STM1-3 was a subadult, indicated by incomplete skeletal fusion during growth.
facts.quote: Se cree que STM1–3 es un subadulto, con características que incluyen la fusión incompleta de partes esqueléticas durante la ontogenia.

facts.statement: The Tianyuraptor holotype does not preserve soft tissues, unlike many other Jehol Group theropod specimens.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Tianyuraptor no conserva tejidos blandos, a diferencia de muchos otros especímenes de terópodos del Grupo Jehol.

facts.statement: The generic name Tianyuraptor combines 'Tianyu', referring to the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature where the holotype is kept, with 'raptor'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico de Tianyuraptor combina el vocablo Tianyu, que hace referencia al Museo Shandong Tianyu de la Naturaleza donde el holotipo está guardado

facts.statement: The specific name 'ostromi' honors John Ostrom for his significant contributions to the study of dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, "ostromi", es en honor a John Ostrom, quien contribuyó enormemente en el estudio de los dromeosáuridos

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Zheng et al. places Tianyuraptor as a basal member of the group containing Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético realizado por Zheng et al. muestra a Tianyuraptor como un miembro basal del grupo que contiene a los dromeosáuridos de Laurasia.

facts.statement: The authors prefer to suggest that Tianyuraptor is considered a short-armed microraptorine.
facts.quote: Los autores entonces prefieren sugerir que Tianyuraptor se considera un microraptorino de brazos cortos

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tianyuraptor is a short-armed microraptorine or a basal member of the clade containing all other Laurasian dromaeosaurids except Microraptorinae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, es también igualmente posible, según lo discutido por Zheng et al., que Tianyuraptor sea de hecho un miembro básico del clado que contiene a todos los otros dromeosáuridos de Laurasia a excepción de Microraptorinae.

facts.statement: The shortened arms, small furcula, and transversely wide coracoid in Tianyuraptor suggest it was not adapted for gliding or aerodynamic flight.
facts.quote: los acortados brazos, la pequeña fúrcula, y el transversalmente ancho coracoides en Tianyuraptor sugiere que no estaba adaptado para el deslizamiento o el vuelo aerodinámico.

facts.statement: Tianyuraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Tianyuraptor lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The type specimen, formally named in 2009, shows features not seen in previously known Northern Hemisphere (Laurasian) dromaeosaurids, but present in Southern Hemisphere (Gondwanan) species and early birds.
